title: Routing and Data Guardrails discovery with Novus FinServ
summary: Discovery call to understand Novus's constraints around sending transactional/PHI-like financial data to hosted inference. Primary concerns: key residency, log redaction, audit evidence, requirements for Private or Dedicated deployment, fallback routing between regions and model variants, and procurement timeline.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Felix Duarte (Redwood Product), Lydia Park (Novus - Head of Data Governance), Marco Silva (Novus CTO), Janelle Ortiz (Novus Compliance), Evan Yoon (Novus Platform)
---
00:00 - Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we are Maya from Redwood, Omar SE, Felix on product, could you do quick intros?
00:14 - Lydia Park: sure, Lydia here, i run data governance at Novus, we have to map where data moves for reg review, especially when it looks like personal financial history, so hi.
00:25 - Marco Silva: Marco, CTO, i'm here to evaluate architecture tradeoffs - latency and cost are big but compliance is blocker.
00:35 - Janelle Ortiz: Janelle, compliance manager, mainly worried about logs and audit trail, retention periods, and whether PHI/PII can hit a hosted service.
00:47 - Maya Chen: understood, that's exactly what we want to cover - how Redwood hosted, dedicated and private fit different profiles; Omar will run through the technical guardrails.
01:02 - Omar Patel: thanks. quick note, i may use acronyms, sorry if i trip up — "S-O-C-2", ISO, KMS, "H S M". so first, high level: hosted = fastest onboarding, Dedicated = reserved GPU pools with network isolation and capacity SLAs, Private = customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
01:26 - Marco Silva: question: for private, does control plane still phone home? we can't have any subprocessors in eu us crossing boundaries without consent.
01:38 - Omar Patel: good call. Private can be deployed in your VPC with no control-plane egress if you choose the air-gap/on-prem option; otherwise the control plane can be configured to restrict egress to specific endpoints. we can provide documentation on subprocessors and subprocess chains.
01:55 - Lydia Park: what's the guarantee on key residency? our legal team wants customer-managed keys and key material never leaves our HSM.
02:06 - Felix Duarte: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration; in Private on-prem we can integrate with your HSM so keys never leave. for Dedicated we can do envelope encryption where root keys live in your KMS and we hold ephemeral wrapping keys.
02:30 - Janelle Ortiz: can you make that part of the contract — prove that no raw model inputs are stored and that logs can be pruned?
02:42 - Maya Chen: yes, we have contractual addenda for log retention and separation; also we offer log-minimization modes where request/response bodies are not persisted. we'll share our SOC2 artifacts and a security pack.
02:58 - Marco Silva: how about streaming responses? we need low latency for a fraud microservice. streaming may mean token-slices leave earlier; does that get logged differently?
03:12 - Omar Patel: streaming is supported; logs are configurable. by default we record metadata and token counts; payload capture is optional and can be disabled for sensitive streams. if you disable payload capture, debugging is harder but compliance improves.
03:34 - Evan Yoon: for network routing, can we force traffic to eu-west region and disallow failover to us-east? our policy is strict.
03:45 - Felix Duarte: yes, you can configure region locking and routing policies; we also support fallback policies, but those are opt-in — if you opt out, the system will return capacity errors rather than failover across regions.
04:02 - Lydia Park: auditability — we need tamper-evident logs for 7 years; does Redwood provide signed audit logs or an export we can ingest into our SIEM?
04:14 - Omar Patel: we provide structured audit logs and can stream them to your S3 or a syslog endpoint; for tamper evidence we support signing and time-stamping; in Private deployments you can keep the logs in your systems and control retention fully.
04:34 - Janelle Ortiz: is there an option to scrub or redact PII before logs get emitted? like regex-based redaction at the edge?
04:44 - Omar Patel: yes, we offer pre-ingest redaction and post-ingest redaction layers — you can provide scrub rules, or we can run a redaction plugin that hashes or masks specific fields. important to test on sample prompts because ML hallucinations can leak.
05:05 - Marco Silva: about model variants — if we use a lighter quantized model for cost, does that change the data residency or tenant isolation?
05:16 - Felix Duarte: model variants are purely software profiles; residency is a deployment property. you can run quantized models in Private or Dedicated and keep all processing in-region. cost/latency will vary with model choices.
05:30 - Lydia Park: any limitations on egress for third-party services? like if a plugin calls out to a credit bureau?
05:40 - Omar Patel: outbound webhooks or tool-calls are controllable: you can allowlist domains, block outbound, or require explicit per-request approval. in hosted we recommend allowlists; in Private you can use internal-only endpoints.
05:56 - Janelle Ortiz: procurement question — timeline for enterprise package with SOC2 evidence and contract wording? we close fiscal Q4.
06:06 - Maya Chen: typical procurement timeline we've seen is 6-10 weeks post-legal review. we'll provide the security package and a draft addendum for data residency and KMS — we can try to accelerate if needed.
06:20 - Marco Silva: benchmark ask — we'd like a small pilot that sends redacted transactional examples and measures 95th percentile latency within our EU region, plus cost estimates. feasible?
06:33 - Omar Patel: absolutely, we can run a pilot on Dedicated EU hosts; will need a small footprint and sample prompts. we'll also provide a test harness to collect token-level timing.
06:48 - Lydia Park: last major blocker: third-party subprocessors list — we need to present to risk committee. can you provide a signed list and SOC artifacts for each?
07:00 - Felix Duarte: we maintain a subprocessors list and can provide SOC2 reports where applicable; for Private on-prem there's no third-party processing.
07:12 - Janelle Ortiz: any red flags on legal around model training? we don't want tuning or fine-tuning on our customer data.
07:23 - Omar Patel: we don't train on customer request data by default; we can set an explicit non-training clause in the contract, and in Private the model weights are static unless you authorize a training run.
07:38 - Evan Yoon: do you offer a kill-switch if we detect exfil? like emergency revoke?
07:46 - Maya Chen: yes, we support tenant-level revocation and can revoke tokens, route to fallback models, and pause traffic; we also have incident response playbooks and can run war games with your ops team.
07:58 - Lydia Park: ok, sounds good. can you send a proposed pilot plan and the security pack?
08:05 - Maya Chen: yes, next steps we will send a one-pager pilot plan, security pack link, and a tailored pricing estimate for Dedicated EU.
---
Notes and imperfections: occasional mis-transcripts: "S-O-C-2" as spelled-out, sometimes "k v cache" instead of KV cache, "H S M" typed, "Anthropic" pronounced with slight hesitation. Some cross-talk at 05:30 between Marco and Omar.
---
End of transcript
action_items: Maya Chen: Share security pack (SOC2, ISO pack), subprocessors list and log redaction docs (due: 2027-07-15)
Omar Patel: Draft pilot test harness and measurement plan for Dedicated EU, include 95p latency test (due: 2027-07-19)
Lydia Park: Provide representative redacted prompt set and compliance checklist for pilot (due: 2027-07-20)
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack link and subprocessors appendix
Set up pilot kick-off: schedule technical kick-off with Novus platform team (Omar)
Legal: exchange draft data residency addendum and KMS clause
